1984.subject: Zoology
1984.text: Assertion : Type I diabetes is caused by destruction of cells of Islets of Langerhans. Reason : Insulin can be taken as injections by Type I patients.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1984.sol: Type I diabetes is an autoimmune disease wherein immune system destroys cells in pancreas called beta cells which make insulin. Insulin is a hormone that helps move sugar from blood into body tissues where cells use it as fuel. Damage to beta cells leads to build up of sugar in blood as cell are not able to utilise it which leads to high blood sugar. Patients having type I diabetes take insulin injections to control blood sugar.

2119.sol: Muscle contraction is brought about by sliding of the actin filaments over myosin filaments. When a muscle fibril contracts, its A band remains constant and I band shortens. H zone also disappears as the actin filaments of both sides in each sarcomere may overlap each other at M line.

57788.subject: Chemistry
57788.text: What is the difference in molar mases of third and fourth homologues of alkane series?
57788.sol: The general formula for alkanes is C_nH_ 2n+2 . The third homologue corresponds to n = 3 , yielding propane C₃H₈ . The molar mass is calculated as (3 12) + (8 1) = 44 g/mol. For the fourth homologue at n = 4 , the formula is butane C₄H₁₀ , with molar mass (4 12) + (10 1) = 58 g/mol. The difference is 58 - 44 = 14 g/mol. This matches the mass of a CH₂ unit ( 12 + 2 = 14 g/mol), which is the constant increment between successive homologues in any homologous series. Final answer: 14 g/mol

71022.subject: Biology
71022.text: We can voluntarily change our pattern of breathing because the respiratory centre __________.
options: in medulla oblongata controls breathing voluntarily
in medulla oblongata has connections with the cerebral cortex
in medulla oblongata and pons are connected with each other
71022.sol: The respiratory centre is primarily located in the medulla oblongata and pons of the brainstem, which controls involuntary breathing. Voluntary control over the pattern of breathing is possible because the respiratory centre has neural connections with the cerebral cortex. The cerebral cortex is the region of the brain responsible for conscious thought and voluntary actions, allowing us to temporarily override the automatic control of breathing. Answer: in medulla oblongata has connections with the cerebral cortex

71117.sol: Actual remains are the intact parts or whole bodies of organisms preserved in their original state, such as preserved bodies of insects embedded in amber. Moulds are formed when an organism decays and leaves an impression of its body parts in the surrounding rock. Casts are formed when the cavities or moulds left by the decayed organism are filled with hardened pieces of mineral matter. 71150.subject: Biology
71150.text: Which one of the following diseases is NOT transmitted by mosquitoes?
71150.sol: Malaria is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito. Filariasis is transmitted by the Culex mosquito. Dengue is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito. Typhoid is a bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi, which is transmitted through contaminated food and water, not by mosquitoes. Answer: Typhoid

71214.subject: Biology
71214.text: Microbial source for the production of enzyme invertase is __________.
71214.sol: Invertase is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of sucrose into a mixture of glucose and fructose, commonly known as invert sugar. The most common and widely used microbial source for the commercial production of the enzyme invertase is the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae . Aspergillus niger is primarily used for the production of citric acid and enzymes like pectinase and amylase. Candida lipolytica is known for the production of lipases. Trichoderma konigii is a source of cellulase enzymes. Answer: Saccharomy

71375.sol: The X and Y chromosomes are structurally different but share short regions of homology known as pseudoautosomal regions (PARs) at their tips. 74130.text: Twinkling of stars is primarily due to the atmospheric
74130.sol: The twinkling of a star is due to the atmospheric refraction of starlight. The starlight, on entering the earth's atmosphere, undergoes refraction continuously before it reaches the earth. 75623.text: Who gifted the Badshah Nama to King George in 1799 ?

79538.subject: Botany
79538.text: The animals with bilateral symmetry in young stage, and radial pentamerous symmetry in the adult stage, belong to the phylum:
79538.sol: In Echinoderms, larval forms possess bilateral symmetry while adults have radial symmetry. Mollusc possess bilateral symmetry. Cnidarian have bilaterally and radial symmetry. Annelid have bilateral symmetry. Caution Class Gastropods (Mollusc) are characterised by their asymmetric body plan, which develops through process called torsion (rotation of visceral organs in anticlockwise direction through an angle of 180^ on the rest of the body during larval development).

79566.subject: Botany
79566.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Morels and truffles are edible delicacies.
Claviceps is a source of many alkaloids and LSD.
Conidia are produced exogenously and ascospores endogenously.
Yeasts have filamentous bodies with long thread-like hyphae.
79566.sol: Yeasts are unicellular eukaryotic fungi with completely different properties from those of bacteria, which are Prokaryotic microorganisms. Yeast contains almost the same organelles of a mature eukaryotic cell. Nucleus, Golgi apparatus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, vacuole, and cytoskeleton are the most important one.

79669.subject: Botany
79669.text: Viruses are no more "alive" than isolated chromosomes because:
options: they require both RNA and DNA
they both require oxygen for respiration
both require the environment of a cell to replicate
79669.sol: Outside of a host cell, viruses do not use any energy. They only become active when they come into contact with a host cell. Once activated, they use the host cell's energy and tools to make more viruses. Because they do not use their own energy, some scientists do not consider them alive. Related Theory The only point favouring the virus as living entities is that they have the ability to reproduce (multiply) within the host by using host's machinery. 80131.subject: Botany
80131.sol: Soyabean belongs to Fabaceae, which shows racemose inflorescence. Brinjal belongs to Solanaceae, which shows cymose inflorescence. Aloe and tulip belongs to Liliaceae family with cymose inflorescence. Related Theory

80189.subject: Botany
80189.text: Read the following four statements, A, B, C and D and select the right OPTION having both correct statements. A. Z secheme of light reaction takes place in presence of PS-I only. B. Only PS-I is functional in cyclic photophosphorylation. C. Cyclic photophosphorylation results into synthesis of ATP and NADPH ₂ . D. Stroma lamellae lack PS-II as well as NADP.
80189.sol: Cyclic photophosphorylation is performed by PS-I only. In this process, an electron expelled by the excited photocentre, ie, P ₇₀₀ is returned to it after passing through a series of electron carriers. PS-I is located on both the non-appressed part of grana thylakoids as well as stroma thylakoids, while PS-II is located in the appressed part of grana thylakoids only, stroma thylakoids lack PS-II.

80321.subject: Botany
80321.sol: Carrageenan is a polysaccharide obtained from the cell wall of Chondrus crispus (Irish moss). It is used in the stabilization of emulsions in paints and cosmetics and in the alcohol and sugar industry. Hydrocolloid carrageen is obtained from Rhodophyceae.

upper oogonium and lower antheridium on the same plant

80509.sol: The structure of the ovule can be studied under the following headings: a) Funicle: The stalk of the ovule by which it remains attached to the placenta. b) Hilum: It is the junction between ovule and funicle or the point of attachment of funiculus to the body of ovule. c) Integument: The one or more protective envelops surrounding the body of the ovule. d) Micropyle: The pore or passage present at the tip of the ovule where the integument is absent. e) Chalaza: Opposite to micropylar end representing the basal part

80544.subject: Botany
80544.text: Nucellar polyembryony is reported in species of
80544.sol: Occurrence of more than one embro in a seed is referred as polyembryony. In many citrus and mango varieties, some of the nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac start dividing, protrude into the embryo-sac and develop into the embryos in such species each ovule contains many embros (nucellar polyembryony).

80844.subject: Chemistry
80844.text: The correct sequence of bond enthalpy of ' C - X bond is:
80844.sol: Bond enthalpy is inversely proportional to the bond length. The bond length order of C - X bond in methyl halides depends on the size of the halogen atom. Bond length order: CH 3 - F < CH 3 - Cl < CH 3 - Br < CH 3 - I Hence, bond enthalpy order is CH 3 - F > CH 3 - Cl > CH 3 - Br > CH 3 - I

83009.subject: Physics
83009.text: Curie temperatures is the temperature above which
83009.sol: Ferromagnetism decreases with rise in temperature. If we heat a ferromagnetic substance, then at a definite temperature the ferromagnetic property of the substance suddenly disappears and the substance becomes paramagnetic. The temperature above which a ferromagnetic substance becomes paramagnetic is called the Curie temperature of the substance. Note: The Curie temperature of iron is 770^ C and that of nickle in 358^ C .

in kidneys as well as eliminated by kidneys
in liver and also eliminated by the same through bile
in the liver, but eliminated mostly through kidneys
84436.sol: In humans, the principal nitrogenous excretory compound (ie, urea) is synthesized in liver by ornithine cycle. 84922.sol: In negative regulation, a repressor molecule binds to the operator of an operon and terminates transcription. The lac operon is a negatively controlled inducible operon, where the inducer molecule is allolactose.

123686.sol: These X-shaped structures, are called chiasmata. In oocytes of some vertebrates, diplotene can last for months or years. The final stage of meiotic prophase I is Diakinesis. This is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata. During this phase the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled to prepare the homologous chromosomes for separation. By the end of diakinesis, the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope also breaks down. Diakinesis represents transition to metaphase.

124426.subject: Botany
124426.text: Ribosomes are particles about 200 Å units in diameter consisting of protein and RNA. The percentage of protein and RNA is respectively
124426.sol: Chemically, ribosomes is made up of r RNA 60 % and protein 40 % . These are known as protein factories as these are the sites for protein synthesis.

124429.subject: Botany
124429.text: Which is substitution of mitochondria in E. coli?
124429.sol: Mesosomes will be equivalent to mitochondria of eukaryotes because of respiratory enzymes present in aerobic bacteria.

124464.subject: Botany
124464.text: Genes for cytoplasmic male sterility in plants are generally located in
124464.sol: Mitochondria are the eukaryotic cell organelles (do not present in prokaryotic cells). These originate from pre-existing mitochondria only. Mitochondria are also known as semi autonomous organelles because they contain a circular, double stranded DNA molecule, RNA and 70 S type of ribosomes. The genes, located outside of nucleus (i.e., within the cytoplasm) also governes some traits, are referred to as plasmogenes or cytoplasmic genes. Cytoplasmic male sterility (i.e., dominance of female cytoplasmic genes over mal

125094.subject: Botany
125094.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Breaking down processes within the living organisms is anabolism Reason: Synthesis of substances in living organisms is catabolism.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
125094.sol: Breaking down processes within the living organisms is catabolism. Synthesis of substances in living organisms is anabolism.

125288.subject: Botany
125288.text: The enzyme responsible for atmospheric nitrogen fixation is :
125288.sol: Enzyme nitrogenase plays a key role in N ₂ fixations and remains active only during anaerobic condition. It is made up of two protein subunits : (i) non-heme iron protein or Fe-protein or dinitrogen reductase. (ii) Iron molybdenum protein or Mo-Fe protein or dinitrogenase.

125653.subject: Botany
125653.text: To fix 6 molecules of CO ₂ in the Calvin cycle, what is the number of ATP molecules utilized strictly in the reduction phase and the regeneration phase, respectively?
125653.sol: In the Calvin cycle, the fixation of a single CO ₂ molecule requires 2 ATP molecules during the reduction phase and 1 ATP molecule during the regeneration of RuBP. For the fixation of 6 molecules of CO ₂ (equivalent to the synthesis of one glucose molecule): ATP utilized in the reduction phase = 6 2 = 12 ATP utilized in the regeneration phase = 6 1 = 6 Therefore, 12 ATP molecules are used in reduction and 6 ATP molecules are used in regeneration. Students often confuse the per CO ₂ requirement (2 and 1) with the to

Zygote, Primary Endosperm, Primary Endosperm Cell
Degenerating cells, Zygote, Degenerating antipodal cells

126012.text: Identify and name w,x,y and z respectively

126038.subject: Botany
126038.text: Select the correct statement for the given figure.
options: The inner wall of the pollen grain is called the exine.
When the pollen grain is mature it contains one cell, the vegetative cell.
In over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at this 2-celled stage. In the remaining species, t
The vegetative cell is smaller, has abundant food reserves and a large irregularly shaped nucleus.
126038.sol: The inner wall of the pollen grain is called the intine. It is a thin and continuous layer made up of cellulose and pectin. The cytoplasm of pollen grain is surrounded by a plasma membrane. When the pollen grain is mature it contains two cells, the vegetative cell and generative cell (Figure 1.5b). The vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus. The generative cell is small and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell. It is spindle shaped with dense cytoplasm

126416.subject: Botany
126416.text: Which of the following statements about Spirogyra is correct?
options: Lateral conjugation takes place in homothallic species.
Scalariform conjugation takes place in homothallic species.
Lateral conjugation takes place in heterothallic species.
The type of conjugation is unrelated to homothallic & heterothallic species.
126416.sol: Sexual reproduction in Spirogyra takes place by the process of conjugation. In Spirogyra, the process of conjugation may be of two types - scalariform conjugation and lateral conjugation. Scalariform conjugation occurs in heterothallic species. Lateral conjugation occurs between the adjacent cells of the same filament of homothallic species of Spirogyra. Lateral conjugation are of two types. They are indirect lateral conjugation (chain type) and direct lateral conjugation.

126433.subject: Botany
126433.text: During unfavourable conditions, the sponges for
126433.sol: Under unfavourable conditions like high temperature, dry condition, sponges body gets divided into numerous small spore like bodies called gemmules to tide over the adverse environmental conditions. Cysts are formed during unfavourable conditions in Amoeba. Spicules are endoskeletons of sponge body.

126509.subject: Botany
126509.text: What is the cause of inhibition in enzyme activity?
126509.sol: With the increase in substrate concentration, the velocity of the enzymatic reaction rises at first. The reaction ultimately reaches a maximum velocity (Vmax) which is not exceeded by any further rise in concentration of the substrate. This is because the enzyme molecules are fewer than the substrate molecules and after saturation of these molecules, there are no free enzyme molecules to bind with the additional substrate molecules. The activity of an enzyme is also sensitive to the presence of specific chemicals t

126685.subject: Botany
126685.text: When you take cells or tissue pieces and grind them with an acid in a mortar and pestle, all the small biomolecules dissolve in the acid. Proteins, polysaccharides and nucleic acids are insoluble in mineral acid and get precipitated. The acid-soluble compounds include amino acids, nucleosides, small sugars etc. When one adds a phosphate group to a nucleoside, one gets another acid-soluble biomolecule called
126685.sol: When one adds a phosphate group to a nucleoside, one gets another acid-soluble biomolecule called Nucleotide.

127052.subject: Botany
127052.text: Cattle ranches are known to causes acute green house effect. This is due to
options: decomposition of organic remains in faeces.
127052.sol: Cattle ranching refers to practice of raising grazing livestock such as cattle or sheep for meat and wool, etc. The area of landscape meant primarily for cattle ranching is called a ranch. The practice has lead to accelerated deforestation and contributed to increased methane gas concentration in atmosphere. Whatever cattle eat; is subjected to the action of methanogens (bacteria) harbouring the stomach (rumen) of cattle. The action of these bacteria on food material produces methane gas which is released through c

127182.subject: Botany
127182.text: How does species richness affect the productivity of an ecosystem according to Tilman's experiments?
options: Increased diversity contributed to lower productivity
Increased diversity contributed to higher productivity
There was no relationship between species richness and productivity
The relationship between species richness and productivity was not determined
127182.sol: A stable community should not show too much variation in productivity from year to year; it must be either resistant or resilient to occasional disturbances (natural or man-made), and it must also be resistant to invasions by alien species. We don’t know how these attributes are linked to species richness in a community, but David Tilman’s long-term ecosystem experiments using outdoor plots provide some tentative answers. Tilman found that plots with more species showed less year-to-year variation in total biomass.

127891.subject: Zoology
127891.text: What do the tissues in the heart collectively contribute to?
options: Complex organ and organ system functions
127891.sol: The basic tissues as you have learnt in earlier classes, organise to form organs which in turn associate to form organ systems in the multicellular organisms. Such an organisation is essential for more efficient and better coordinated activities of millions of cells constituting an organism . Each organ in our body is made of one or more type of tissues. For example, our heart consists of all the four types of tissues, i.e., epithelial, connective, muscular and neural. We also notice, after some careful study that

128110.subject: Zoology
128110.text: Read the following statements carefully: A. All cells in epithelium are held together with abundant intercellular material. B. Tight junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together. C. Gap junctions facilitate communication by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells. D. Specialised junctions provide only functional links between individual cells in animal tissues. How many of the given statements
128110.sol: Statement A is incorrect because all cells in epithelium are held together with little (not abundant) intercellular material. Statement B is incorrect because adhering junctions (not tight junctions) perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together. Tight junctions stop substances from leaking across a tissue. Statement C is correct as gap junctions facilitate cell communication by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells. Statement D is incorrect because specialised junctions provide both structural and fu

128364.subject: Zoology
128364.text: What is the role of glucagons in maintaining glucose homeostasis?
options: Maintains glucose homeostasis jointly with insulin
Does not play a role in maintaining glucose homeostasis
128364.sol: Insulin is a peptide hormone, which plays a major role in the regulation of glucose homeostasis. Insulin acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes (cells of adipose tissue), and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation. As a result, there is a rapid movement of glucose from blood to hepatocytes and adipocytes resulting in decreased blood glucose levels (hypoglycemia). Insulin also stimulates conversion of glucose to glycogen (glycogenesis) in the target cells. The glucose homeostasis in blood is thus mainta

128374.subject: Zoology
128374.text: What are the effects of androgens on male sexual behaviour?
128374.sol: Androgens regulate the development, maturation and functions of the male accessory sex organs like epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, prostate gland, urethra etc. These hormones stimulate muscular growth, growth of facial and axillary hair, aggressiveness, low pitch of voice etc. Androgens play a major stimulatory role in the process of spermatogenesis (formation of spermatozoa). Androgens act on the central neural system and influence the male sexual behaviour (libido). These hormones produce anabolic (sy

128398.subject: Zoology
128398.text: What is the role of hormones in target tissue metabolism and physiological functions?
options: Hormones stimulate target tissue metabolism and physiological functions
Hormones inhibit target tissue metabolism and physiological functions
Hormones regulate target tissue metabolism and physiological functions
Hormones do not have any effect on target tissue metabolism and physiological functions
128398.sol: Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors located in the target tissues only. Hormone receptors present on the cell membrane of the target cells are called membrane-bound receptors and the receptors present inside the target cell are called intracellular receptors, mostly nuclear receptors (present in the nucleus). Binding of a hormone to its receptor leads to the formation of a hormone-receptor complex (Figure 19.5 a, b). Each receptor is specific to

128708.subject: Zoology
128708.sol: Vitamin B₆ , also called pyridoxine is widely distributed in cereal grains, yeast, liver, milk, etc. It is a constituent of a coenzyme (pyridoxal phosphate) involved in amino acid metabolism. Deficiency causes retarded growth, dermatitis, convulsions, and other symptoms.

128852.subject: Zoology
128852.text: What type of circulation do humans have?
128852.sol: Human circulatory system, also called the blood vascular system consists of a muscular chambered heart, a network of closed branching blood vessels and blood, the fluid which is circulated.

128949.subject: Zoology
128949.text: What is the other blood grouping system besides the A, B, AB and O systems?
options: The presence or absence of antigen C
The presence or absence of antigen D
The presence or absence of Rh factor
The presence or absence of antigen E
128949.sol: Another antigen, the Rh antigen similar to one present in Rhesus monkeys (hence Rh), is also observed on the surface of RBCs of majority (nearly 80 per cent) of humans. Such individuals are called Rh positive (Rh+ve) and those in whom this antigen is absent are called Rh negative (Rh-ve). An Rh-ve person, if exposed to Rh+ve blood, will form specific antibodies against the Rh antigens. Therefore, Rh group should also be matched before transfusions.

128987.subject: Zoology
128987.text: Blood Vessel Characteristic A. Arteries 1. Carry blood away from the heart B. Veins 2. Carry blood toward the heart C. Capillaries 3. Small vessels connecting capillaries to veins D. Venules 4. Site of nutrient and gas exchange
128987.sol: Arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart (except the pulmonary artery). Veins carry deoxygenated blood back toward the heart (except the pulmonary vein). Capillaries are the site of exchange of gases, nutrients, and waste products between blood and tissues. Venules are small vessels that collect blood from capillaries and deliver it to veins.

129168.subject: Zoology
129168.text: In which blood group antigens are absent?
129168.sol: Person with blood group 'O' has no antigen on his RBC but has both the antibodies (i.e., a and b) in his plasma. Whereas a person with blood group ' A B ' has both antigens but no antibody. Due to this blood group ' O ' is universal donor and blood group ' A B ' is universal acceptor.

130129.subject: Zoology
130129.text: Oxygen dissociation curve of haemoglobin is
130129.sol: Oxygen haemoglobin dissociation curve gives the relationship between the saturation of haemoglobin and oxygen tension. The curve obtained by plotting the per cent saturation of Hb against time is sigmoid, at 38^ C and pH 7.4. Dissociation of oxyhaemoglobin can be promoted by rise in the body temperature and low pH ( . high . CO ₂ ) .

He must know how to sort out the news

130227.subject: Zoology
130227.text: What is the function of troponin in muscle contraction?
options: It regulates the release of calcium ions
It forms cross bridges with myosin
It masks the active sites for myosin
130227.sol: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system (CNS) via a motor neuron.The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plate.When a neural signal reaches the neuromuscular junction, it releases a neurotransmitter (Acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of a muscle fiber is called the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plat

130430.subject: Zoology
130430.text: Which one of the following options is incorrect?
options: Hinge joint – between humerus and pectoral girdle
Pivot joint – between atlas, axis and occipital condyle
Saddle joint – between carpal and metacar- pals of thumb
130430.sol: A hinge joint allows movement in one plane. Joint between the humerus and pectoral girdle is an example of a ball and socket joint.

130518.subject: Zoology
130518.text: Epiphyseal plates at the extremities of long bones help in
130518.sol: Epiphyseal plate is found between diaphysis and epiphysis. It contributes in the elongation of bone during growth period.

130603.subject: Zoology
130603.text: When are MTPs considered relatively safe?
options: During the first trimester (up to 12 weeks of pregnancy)
130603.sol: MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e., upto 12 weeks of pregnancy. Second trimester abortions are much more riskier. One disturbing trend observed is that a majority of the MTPs are performed illegally by unqualified quacks which are not only unsafe but could be fatal too. Another dangerous trend is the misuse of amniocentesis to determine the sex of the unborn child. Frequently, if the foetus is found to be female, it is followed by MTP- this is totally against what is legal.

130697.subject: Zoology
130697.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. Professional expertise and material support is not recquired for various action plans to attain reproductive health 2. Statutory ban on amniocentesis has been implemented to legally check female foeticides 3. Amniocentesis is used to check for genetic disorders 4. Amniocentesis can be used to detect cleft plate
130697.sol: Successful implementation of various action plans to attain reproductive health requires strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support. These are essential to provide medical assistance and care to people in reproduction-related problems.

130709.subject: Zoology
130709.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Condom is made of polythene 2. Saheli is an once a week oral contraceptive pill 3. Testosterone-estrogen is a contraceptive method used by females 4. Copper releasing IUDs are CuT and Cu17 5. Spermicidal creams increase the efficiency of IUDs
130709.sol: Saheli–the new oral contraceptive for the females contains a non-steroidal preparation. It is a ‘once a week’ pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value.

131102.subject: Zoology
131102.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The secondary follicles soon transforms into a tertiary follicle which is characterised by a fluid filled cavity called antrum. 2. The theca layer is organised into an inner theca interna and an outer theca externa. 3. The tertiary follicle further changes into the mature follicle or Graafian follicle. 4. The tertiary oocyte forms a new membrane called z
131102.sol: The secondary follicles soon transforms into a tertiary follicle which is characterised by a fluid filled cavity called antrum. The theca layer is organised into an inner theca interna and an outer theca externa. The tertiary follicle further changes into the mature follicle or Graafian follicle. The secondary oocyte forms a new membrane called zona pellucida surrounding it.

131106.subject: Zoology
131106.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. During luteal phase, the primary follicles in the ovary grow to become a fully mature Graafian follicle and simultaneously the endometrium of uterus regenerates through proliferation. 2. The changes in the ovary and the uterus are induced by changes in the level of progesterone. 3. The secretion of gonadotrophins increases gradually during the follicular
131106.sol: During follicular phase, the primary follicles in the ovary grow to become a fully mature Graafian follicle and simultaneously the endometrium of uterus regenerates through proliferation. The changes in the ovary and the uterus are induced by changes in the level of pituitary and ovarian Hormones.The secretion of gonadotrophins increases gradually during the follicular phase, and stimulates follicular development as well as secretion of estrogens by the growing follicles. Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximu

131152.subject: Zoology
131152.sol: Male and female gametes are haploid

131282.subject: Zoology
131282.text: Given below are some developmental milestones during human embryonic development: A. Separation of eyelids B. Formation of the heart C. First movements of the foetus D. Development of limbs and digits E. Formation of most major organ systems Choose the correct chronological sequence of their appearance during pregnancy:
131282.sol: According to the NCERT textbook, the chronological order of embryonic development is as follows: After one month of pregnancy, the embryo's heart is formed (B). By the end of the second month, the foetus develops limbs and digits (D). By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), most of the major organ systems are formed (E). During the fifth month, the first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are observed (C). By the end of about 24 weeks (end of second trimester), the body is covered with fin

131386.subject: Zoology
131386.text: The immediate cause of induction of ovulation in female is the large plasma surge of
131386.sol: Ovulation takes place on 14th day of cycle, concentration of LH is highest on 14th day because it has to break the Graafian follicle so as to release the ovum later if the concentration of estrogen and progesterone decrease there is lose of internal lining of uterus and menstural bleeding start.

132292.subject: Zoology
options: Increase in a whole set of chromosomes
132292.sol: The chromosomal disorders on the other hand are caused due to absence or excess or abnormal arrangement of one or more chromosomes. Failure of segregation of chromatids during cell division cycle results in the gain or loss of a chromosome(s), called aneuploidy. For example, Down’s syndrome results in the gain of extra copy of chromosome 21. Similarly, Turner’s syndrome results due to loss of an X chromosome in human females. Failure of cytokinesis after telophase stage of cell division results in an increase in a

133001.subject: Zoology
133001.text: Which of the following structures is homologous to the wing of a bird?
133001.sol: When two or more organs or structures are basically similar to each other in construction but are modified to perform different functions, they are said to be serially homologous. Flipper of the whale is homologous to the wing of a bird.

133067.subject: Zoology
133067.text: Assertion : The earliest organisms that appeared on the Earth were non-green and presumably anaerobes. Reason : The first autotrophic organisms were the chemoautotrophs that never released oxygen.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
133067.sol: The first living organisms originated among organic molecules and in oxygen free atmosphere. They presumably obtained energy by fermentation of some of these organic molecules. They were non-green and anaerobes (capable of respiring in absence of oxygen). They depended on the existing organic molecules for their nutrition, hence they were heterotrophs. Then came autotrophs when the supply of existing organic molecules were exhausted. These organisms were capable of producing their own organic molecules by chemosynt

133254.subject: Zoology
133254.sol: The acronym AIDS stands for Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, which indicates a deficiency of the immune system acquired during an individual's lifetime. People who are at high risk of getting HIV infection include individuals with multiple sexual partners, drug addicts who take drugs intravenously, individuals who require repeated blood transfusions, and children born to an HIV-infected mother.The spread of HIV infection is due to conscious behavior patterns and not due to natural causes or poor monitoring.NACO

133480.subject: Zoology
133480.text: How does the transmission of Malaria take place?
133480.sol: Plasmodium, or malarial parasite, is communicated to a healthy person from a patient when bitten by a female Anopheles mosquito

133670.subject: Zoology
133670.text: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
133670.sol: Trichomonas vaginalis is a flagellate found in vagina of female (humans) causing vaginalis. It leads to burning sensation, itching and frothy vaginal discharge. Leishmaniasis or kala-azar is caused by Leishmania donovani. It is characterised by the presence of cutaneous oriental roses along with fever.

133699.subject: Zoology
133699.text: The larvicidial fish used in biocontrol of mosquitoes
133699.sol: Gambusia is an exotic fish feeds on the larvae of mosquito. Now-a-days it is widely used to eradicate mosquito.

133704.subject: Zoology
133704.text: Where can microbes be found, even though no other life-form exists?
133704.sol: Microbes are present everywhere – in soil, water, air, inside our bodies and that of other animals and plants. They are present even at sites where no other life-form could possibly exist–sites such as deep inside the geysers (thermal vents) where the temperature may be as high as 100 degree C, deep in the soil, under the layers of snow several metres thick, and in highly acidic environments.

133908.subject: Zoology
133908.text: Fungi/Bacteria Application A. Blue-green algae 1. Antibiotic B. Bacillus subtilis 2. Biofertilizer C. Penicillin 3. Probiotic D. Lactic acid bacteria 4. Protease production
133908.sol: Blue-green algae act as a biofertilizer. Bacillus subtilis is used in protease production. Penicillin is an antibiotic. Lactic acid bacteria are used as probiotics.

134215.subject: Zoology
134215.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Animals that have had their DNA manipulated to possess and express an extra gene are known as Transgenic animals. Reason: Transgenic rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish have been produced, although over 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals are mice.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
134215.sol: Animals that have had their DNA manipulated to possess and express an extra gene are known as Transgenic animals. Transgenic rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish have been produced, although over 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals are mice.

134512.subject: Zoology
134512.text: What is used to remove proteins from the mixture of released macromolecules?
134512.sol: Since the DNA is enclosed within the membranes, we have to break the cell open to release DNA along with other macromolecules such as RNA, proteins, polysaccharides and also lipids. This can be achieved by treating the bacterial cells/plant or animal tissue with enzymes such as lysozyme (bacteria), cellulase (plant cells), chitinase (fungus). You know that genes are located on long molecules of DNA interwined with proteins such as histones. The RNA can be removed by treatment with ribonuclease whereas proteins can

134820.subject: Zoology
134820.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): In recombinant DNA technology, it is essential to subject the restriction digest to agarose gel electrophoresis before performing PCR amplification of the gene of interest. Reason (R): Restriction endonucleases cleave the source DNA into multiple fragments, and gel electrophoresis is required to is
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
134820.sol: In recombinant DNA technology, the isolation of the desired DNA fragment is a crucial step that follows the cutting of DNA by restriction endonucleases. Restriction enzymes digest the source DNA into a mixture of multiple fragments. To amplify the specific gene of interest using PCR, this desired fragment must first be separated from the rest of the genomic DNA fragments. This separation is achieved using agarose gel electrophoresis, where fragments are separated based on their size. The desired band is then cut ou

135357.subject: Zoology
135357.text: How many of the following statements are correct? (A) The prickly pear cactus introduced into Australia in the early 1920s was brought under control by a cactus-feeding predator moth. (B) In the rocky intertidal communities of the American Pacific coast, removal of the starfish Pisaster resulted in the extinction of more than 10 species of invertebrates due to interspecific competition. (C) Cuscuta, a parasitic plant
135357.sol: Statement (A) is correct. Predators act as biological control agents, as seen with the prickly pear cactus and its predator moth. Statement (B) is correct. Predators help maintain species diversity by reducing the intensity of interspecific competition among competing prey species. Removal of Pisaster caused the extinction of invertebrate species due to increased competition. Statement (C) is correct. Parasites evolve special adaptations such as the loss of unnecessary sense organs or photosynthetic ability. Cuscut

6a13e466688ac6d0667aad25.subject: Chemistry

The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of neutrons present in its nucleus. C. All isotopes of a given element possess the same number of protons. D. Cathode rays consist of positively charged particles. E. The mass of a neutron is slightly greater than the mass of a pr
6a13e466688ac6d0667aad25.sol: Statement A is correct. Isobars are atoms of different elements that have the same mass number but different atomic numbers. Statement B is incorrect. The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of protons present in its nucleus, not the number of neutrons. Statement C is correct. Isotopes of a given element have the same atomic number, which means they possess the same number of protons, but they differ in the number of neutrons. Statement D is incorrect. Cathode rays consist of electrons, which are neg

6a16f3297cfacf7984f86748.subject: Biology
6a16f3297cfacf7984f86748.text: Match List I with List II: List I List II A Founder effect I Single step large mutation B Saltation II More individuals acquire mean character value C Stabilising selection III Original drifted population becomes a new species D Directional selection IV More individuals acquire value other than the mean character value Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
6a16f3297cfacf7984f86748.sol: Founder effect occurs when a small group of individuals breaks off from a larger population to establish a colony, and the original drifted population becomes a new species. Thus, A matches with III. Saltation was proposed by Hugo de Vries and refers to a single step large mutation that causes speciation. Thus, B matches with I. Stabilising selection is a type of natural selection where more individuals acquire the mean character value, leading to a narrower peak and reduced variation. Thus, C matches with II. Dire

6a1bb6bf107bf677676d9f7d.subject: Biology
6a1bb6bf107bf677676d9f7d.text: What is the net gain of ATP molecules synthesized directly through substrate-level phosphorylation during the complete aerobic respiration of one molecule of glucose?
6a1bb6bf107bf677676d9f7d.sol: During the complete aerobic respiration of one molecule of glucose, substrate-level phosphorylation occurs in two main stages: In glycolysis, 4 ATP molecules are produced directly, but 2 ATP molecules are consumed in the preparatory phase. Thus, the net gain of ATP from substrate-level phosphorylation in glycolysis is 2 ATP. In the Krebs cycle, 1 molecule of GTP (which is equivalent to ATP) is produced per turn during the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinic acid. Since one glucose molecule yields two molecules o

95448.subject: Botany
95448.text: Which of the following options contains a set of protochordates?
95448.sol: Subphyla Urochordata and Cephalochordata are often referred to as protochordates and are exclusively marine. In Urochordata, the notochord is present only in larval tail, while in Cephalochordata, it extends from head to tail region and is persistent throughout their life. 95777.sol: Ascomycetes are also called sac-fungi. They may be multicellular, e.g., Penicillium, or rarely unicellular, e.g., yeast (Saccharomyces). They are saprophytic, decomposers, parasitic or coprophilous (growing on dung). Mycelium is branched and septate. Sexual spores are called ascospores which are produced endogenously in sac like asci (singular ascus). These asci are arranged in different types of fruiting bodies called ascocarps. 96355.subject: Botany
96355.text: How many chromosomes will the cell have at G1, after S, and after M-phase respectively, if it has 21 chromosomes at interphase?
96355.sol: If an interphase cell has 22 chromosomes than the cell at G1 has 22 chromosomes. In S phase on duplication of DNA occurs but chromosome number remains unchanged, thus cell at S phase will also have 22 chromosomes. After the M - phase or mitosis phase equal division occurs and two identical cells are produced having 22 chromosomes each.

96472.subject: Botany
96472.text: In how many of the following, primary succession will occur? (Abandoned farmland, newly created pond, bare rock, burnt forest)
options: Newly created ponds, bare rock, bandoned farmlands and burnt forests
Newly created ponds and bare rock
Abandoned farmlands, bare rocks and burnt forests
96472.sol: When succession occurs in an area where no living organism ever existed; it is called primary succession and when it takes place in areas that have lost all living organisms that had existed there; it is called secondary succession. Newly created ponds, bare rock are examples of primary succession. Abandoned farmlands and burnt forests are examples of secondary succession.

96748.text: Determine the element from the following description. (I) Activate enzyme of photosynthesis and respiration (II) Involved in the synthesis of DNA and RNA (III) Help to maintain structure of ribosome
96748.sol: Magnesium is one of the macronutrient significant for plant growth and development. Magnesium activates the enzymes RubisCO and PEP carboxylase which are important in photosynthesis and respiration process. It is a constituent of the green pigment chlorophyll and actively involved in making DNA and RNA. It is also required to maintain the integrity of ribosome.

96814.subject: Botany
96814.sol: The root cap's primary function is enhancing direct root growth by reducing friction against the soil, sensing gravity and protecting root meristem. In hydrophytes, the root system will be of a fibrous type and hence, the root pockets are present, whereas the root caps are absent, e.g., Eichhornia, Pistia, Lemna . Pandanus, Pothos and Ficus are plants that grow on soil.

96835.subject: Botany

96835.sol: In some seeds, the endosperm is retained in the form of a food storing tissue. These seeds are called endospermic seeds which are found in rice, barley, coffee, and castor. The seeds in which the endosperm is completely consumed by the developing embryo. Such seeds are called non-endospermic seeds which include sunflower, bean, and gram.

97358.sol: Gibberellic acid (GA3) was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form. All GAs are acidic. They produce a wide range of physiological responses in the plants. Their ability to cause an increase in length of axis is used to increase the length of grapes stalks. 97562.subject: Botany
97562.text: In Pinus , male and female cones occur on
options: same branch of the same plant
different branches of the same plant
97562.sol: Pinus is a gymnosperm which produces cones bearing the male and the female reproductive gametes. The male cones are smaller and are found on the lower branches of the tree and the female cones larger than the male cones are on the upper branches of the same tree. Therefore the cones occur on the different branches of the same plant.

97630.subject: Botany
97630.text: Primary acceptor in TCA cycle is
97630.sol: In the TCA cycle, a four-carbon compound (oxaloacetate) condenses with a two-carbon acetyl unit to yield a six-carbon tricarboxylic acid (citrate). It is the gateway to the aerobic metabolism of any molecule that can be transformed into an acetyl group or dicarboxylic acid. The cycle is also an important source of precursors, not only for the storage forms of fuels, but also for the building blocks of many other molecules such as amino acids, nucleotide bases, cholesterol and porphyrin.
